scope: source-only harness preparation; no compiler, JVM, DSO, or test process was run
coverage_added: A separate test-only translation unit includes each exact production vendored core and calls its qsort_ implementation with max_iters=0, forcing the shared bounded heap fallback. Compile it once with RANGE_SORT_FALLBACK_E and once with RANGE_SORT_FALLBACK_U; unique exported symbols allow both objects in one harness.
Fallback oracle case sorts a nonzero-low 73-element interval while checking prefix and suffix sentinels.

Native guard harness now covers INT32_MIN low, INT32_MAX high and empty bounds, null stack-limit, null array, low-stack and existing invalid size/order declines; every array-backed decline checks no mutation.

Both normal kernels get guard-page/oracle coverage at sizes 512..519, 1023..1025, 4095..4097, 8191..8192 with equal, two-value, extreme, reverse, organ-pipe, and deterministic random patterns. Nonzero-low tests cover lower-edge-near and upper-edge-abutting placements, with surrounding canaries.
edge_limit: A nonzero low index cannot have array+low abut a protected lower page while array itself remains a valid readable pointer: the array base must point into accessible memory. The harness therefore uses exact lower-guard adjacency for low=0 and low=7 with the selected interval 7 words inside the lower page, plus a nonzero-low interval ending exactly at the upper guard. It verifies that surrounding prefix/suffix words remain unchanged.

allocation_audit.claim: Guard pages and oracle/canary checks do not establish absence of native allocation.
allocation_audit.source_observation: The bounded entry and its visible kernel wrapper contain no explicit allocation; this is a source observation, not a whole-closure or binary proof.
allocation_audit.future_requirement: Before ordinary execution, inspect the built E/U dynamic imports and retained disassembly for allocator/loader calls and audit all invoked source paths. If allocation-free behavior must be proved, use a separately designed complete allocation interception or binary/source proof; this harness does not intercept allocations.
allocation_audit.why_no_harness_interposition: Overriding malloc/new in this standalone harness would not reliably cover allocator entry points or allocations from all statically/dynamically linked library paths, and would alter the diagnostic process. It is not treated as sound proof.

JNI_witness_review.result: The forwarding witness exports the same four-argument C entry ABI and XssActivation JNI counter/reset names; constructor-only dlopen/dlsym resolution occurs before calls, and the leaf path only counts and forwards.
JNI_witness_review.limits: Counter reads are diagnostic and happen outside measured runs. A successful forwarding counter proves the normal real DSO entry ran, not absence of allocations or correctness under Java data races.

future_compile_argv.toolchain: Use only the GCC g++ selected by the approved Linux x86_64 JDK toolchain; do not substitute Clang. Resolve GXX to that exact executable before the future authorized compile.
future_compile_argv.execution_constraint: These are future argv only. No invocation is authorized by this review. The harness then needs exactly two immutable E/U DSOs as argv and feature gating for AVX512F/DQ/VL, AVX2, and POPCNT.

product_state: No product source changes were made in this update. Prior root-owned worktree edits remain uncommitted and preserved.
